title: The Subjectivity of Respect in Police Traffic Stops: Modeling Community Perspectives in Body-Worn Camera Footage

bias_targets.methodology: Using mixed-effects regression models to analyze how annotators' prior lived experiences (e.g., police-affiliated, justice-system-impacted, or non-affiliated) influence their subjective ratings and rationales of respect.
Incorporating the annotators' race as well as the perceived race of the police officers and civilian drivers into mixed-effects models to evaluate its impact on respect judgments.
Incorporating the annotators' gender and the perceived gender of the officers and drivers into mixed-effects models to assess its effect on respect annotations.
Using mixed-effects regression models to evaluate whether the age of the annotators or the perceived age of the officers and drivers significantly influences respect ratings.
Evaluating how the presence of a perceived foreign accent in either the police officer or the civilian driver affects annotators' respect ratings through mixed-effects regression.

Analyzing the effect of perceived socioeconomic attributes, such as the civilian's clothing and car type (e.g., middle-class vs. working-class vehicle), on respect annotations using mixed-effects models.
Including perceived physical characteristics of the interactants, such as height, as control variables in mixed-effects models to see if they influence respect evaluations.
